title: Rotorworks — Cipher Workbench
description: A working three-wheel Enigma with a live signal path, five classical ciphers, and a bench that breaks Caesar and Vigenère.
concept: Three rooms of one machine shop. The Enigma room runs historical wheels I–V, ring settings, a ten-cable plugboard and both reflectors, drawing the circuit your last keypress took from keyboard to reflector and back to the lamp. The Classical room enciphers with Caesar, Vigenère, Playfair, rail fence and Atbash, each with a diagram of why it works. The Analysis room counts letters, measures the index of coincidence, ranks all 26 Caesar shifts by chi-square and recovers a Vigenère key column by column — one tap drops the solution back into the workbench.
features: Enigma I: wheels I–V in three slots, ring settings, start key, UKW-B/C, ten plugboard cables with correct double-stepping
Animated signal path through plugboard, three wheels and the reflector, with the lamp that lights at the end
Five classical ciphers, each with its own live diagram: shifted alphabet, key stream, 5×5 keyed square, zigzag rails
Cryptanalysis bench: frequency chart against English, index of coincidence, chi-square Caesar ranking, Vigenère key-length and key recovery, one-tap apply
Export the full transcript as .txt and the key sheet as .json; copy a share link that carries the whole machine in the URL; presets and autosave in localStorage

interaction.mouse: Drag the sliders, pick wheels and rings, click two plugboard letters to cable them together.
interaction.click: Tap the on-screen keyboard to type into the machine; tap a cracked candidate to apply it to the workbench.
interaction.touch: Full touch layout — tabs, rotor nudges, plugboard and keyboard are all tap targets; the rail docks to the bottom.
interaction.keyboard: Type any letter anywhere outside a field and it goes into the machine; Backspace rewinds a letter.
